card: Allocates unused LevelDB block cache budget to write buffers on 64-bit systems. Currently, CDBWrapper reserves half of each database cache budget for LevelDB's block cache, but LevelDB's 64-bit mmap path treats uncompressed table blocks as non-cacheable, leaving the cache empty. This PR sets the block cache size to zero and doubles write_buffer_size on 64-bit systems while preserving the 32-bit allocation scheme. Author benchmarks for chainstate reindexing showed neutral performance impact across multiple architectures.
evidence: Commit ecb530c63d and PR description note that LevelDB serves table blocks directly from mmap-backed files without compression on 64-bit systems and marks them non-cacheable, leaving the block cache unused.
PR description benchmarks running `reindex-chainstate` up to height 954459 across x86_64 (Ryzen, i9) and aarch64 (Raspberry Pi 5) showed no meaningful runtime difference (within 1-2% variance).
problem: On 64-bit systems, Bitcoin Core reserves half of each LevelDB cache budget for LevelDB's block cache, but because uncompressed tables are read via mmap, LevelDB marks those blocks non-cacheable and never populates the block cache, effectively stranding that memory budget.
scope_notes: Very small diff (+5/-2) localized to `GetOptions` in `src/dbwrapper.cpp`.
summary: Adjust LevelDB cache allocations in CDBWrapper on 64-bit builds by setting the block cache capacity to zero and doubling the write buffer size. Retain the existing block cache and write buffer proportions on 32-bit platforms where mmap is disabled.
